subject: Private stack pricing: staged entitlements, support banding & migration credit request

Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment packaging questions and migration credit

Hi Naomi / Marissa,

Thanks for the deck this morning — the architecture looks promising. Procurement asked me to get clarity on a few commercial items before we loop them into a formal SOW. High-level asks from my side: 

- Can you break out the licensing model for a multi-cluster private stack (us-east + eu-west) — specifically node vs. seat entitlements and whether platform fee is per-cluster or per-customer?
- We need a clear support tier matrix (SLOs / response windows) and what’s included in each band.
- We're pushing for a one-time implementation/migration credit to offset our pilot integration costs — ballpark we’re looking at $50k-$100k. What's Redwood willing to offer for a 12-month committed consumption/seat minimum?
- Payment terms: ScaleHealth prefers Net 60. Will that be acceptable for a first-year enterprise agreement?

Attaching our requirements summary and a short procurement checklist. Could we hop on a 30-min call next week to align?

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Jones
Head of Data Products, ScaleHealth

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>

Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment packaging questions and migration credit

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. Quick replies below and attaching our pricing sheet so you have line-level detail.

Short answers up front:
- Licensing: we offer node-based entitlements for private stacks (node = GPU host). Seat licensing is available as an add-on for access management but core unit economics are node-based. Platform fee is charged at the customer level (single annual platform fee) and covers control plane, telemetry retention, and rollout tooling. Multi-cluster (us-east + eu-west) is priced as a single account with regional add-ons (minor uplift per additional region).
- Support tiers: Bronze / Silver / Gold. Bronze = business hours, 24-hr SLA for P1; Silver = 24/7 basic on-call, 8-hr P1; Gold = 24/7 SRE + 2-hr P1 response and monthly 1:1 reviews. Detailed matrix in tab 3 of the attached sheet.
- Migration credit: we can consider a one-time implementation credit in exchange for a 12-month minimum committed spend. Options in the sheet show scaled credit amounts depending on committed monthly baseline.
- Payment terms: standard is Net 30 for first-year enterprise customers; Net 60 possible with an associated credit holdback or reduced migration credit. E.g., Net 60 + $25k holdback / release on invoice milestones.

Proposed next steps: 30-min call Mon/Tue next week. If you prefer, we can provide a formal counter-proposal in writing with numbers after that call.

Attaching: redwood_vpc_pricing_sheet_v3.xlsx (xlsx)

—
Naomi Feldman
Head of Commercial, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai

- Platform fee: ScaleHealth’s finance is pushing to either exclude the platform fee for the first 12 months or to reduce it by at least 60% as part of the pilot commitment.
- Migration credit: we are targeting $75k minimum given the integration work across our data mesh and security validation. That would be tied to a 12-month committed baseline of 100 nodes equivalent (we can share usage profile during the call).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can flex on platform fee and the mechanics for the migration credit? If you can get close to the numbers above, procurement will fast-track the DocuSign.

Notes and counterproposal (pricing team):

Summary assumptions: 100-node equivalent = 12-month committed baseline, mixed node sizes (A100 and 4090-equivalent), expected monthly utilization >= 40% for A100 class.

Counteroffer (clean bullets for Naomi to send):
- Platform fee: amortize the standard platform fee over 18 months for cash impact (effective ~44% reduction in Y1 cash out). This preserves list price while easing their cash flow.
- Migration credit: offer a $60k one-time migration credit applied to the first invoice if ScaleHealth signs a 12-month 100-node commit. $75k possible only if they accept a 24-month commit or prepay 50% of year 1.
- Payment terms: Net 60 accepted with staged payment schedule: 30% upfront, 40% at go-live, 30% at 90 days. We will retain a $25k holdback against the last payment if Net 60 is used without prepay.
- Support tier: map ScaleHealth’s expected use to Silver by default; Gold add-on +$18k/mo for 24/7 SRE and 2-hr P1 response.
- Regional uplift: +7% per additional active region to cover cross-region control-plane replication and interconnect.

Attachments: pricing-counter-offer-v1.pdf (pdf) — shows line-item math and amortization schedule.

My suggested negotiation language for Naomi to send: concise, conditional bullets, call out milestones for holdback release and a clear acceptance path (DocuSign link to primary commercial terms + SOW).

Marissa
Pricing Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Private deployment packaging questions and migration credit — Redwood counterproposal

Emma — thanks for the clarity and for looping procurement. Based on internal ops and pricing review, here’s a concise counterproposal for ScaleHealth to review: 

1) Platform fee: we will amortize the standard platform fee over 18 months to reduce Year 1 cash by ~44%. This keeps the list price intact but eases your cash flow.

2) Migration credit: we can commit to a $60,000 one-time migration credit applied to the first invoice conditioned on a 12-month committed baseline of 100-node equivalent. If ScaleHealth prefers $75,000 credit, that is available only with a 24-month commit or a 50% prepayment of Year 1.

3) Payment terms: Net 60 acceptable with the staged payment schedule you proposed (30% upfront, 40% at go-live, 30% at 90 days). Because Net 60 increases our credit exposure, we will retain a $25,000 holdback to be released on completion of go-live milestones (detailed in SOW).

4) Support: we recommend Silver as the default tier. If you need Gold (2-hr P1, dedicated SRE rotation), that is a $18k/mo add-on.

5) Regional uplift: additional active regions will have a +7% uplift to cover cross-region control-plane replication costs.

If that sounds reasonable, I will send a DocuSign with the commercial term sheet and a link to the SOW for acceptance. Once signed, our delivery team will schedule an internal kickoff and provide a go-live milestone plan for holdback release.

Next steps: confirm whether you want to proceed with 12- or 24-month commit and we’ll generate the DocuSign.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
